title: Compatibility with finite scalar extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E\subset E'$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the completed integral coefficient categories and their raw rationalizations $\Dbc(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with no Karoubi envelope. Derived scalar extension means integral change of completed coefficient rings followed by scalar localization. Then it defines an exact functor
$$T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:\Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$, balancing of derived tensor specifies an exact natural isomorphism
$$a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.$$
The associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four nested fields. There are canonical natural shift comparisons
$$\sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]$$
commuting with these associators.

Write $C_{E'/E,T}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E',T}$ for the integral ambient scalar-extension functor; its constructible restriction and rationalization is $T_{E'/E,T}$. For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ between schemes satisfying the same scheme hypotheses, there are coherent comparisons on ambient derived-complete integral categories
$$C_{E'/E,Y}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,X},\qquad
C_{E'/E,Y'}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp},\mathcal O_{E'}}C_{E'/E,Y}.$$
Their restrictions and rationalizations are comparisons on $\Dbc$ whenever the displayed operations preserve those constructible categories; no preservation assertion for arbitrary $f$ is implicit. Here ordinary direct image is the ringed-topos derived direct image, and completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For a cartesian square $(f,f',g,g')$ whose four schemes satisfy the stated hypotheses, the exchange is the canonical ambient ringed-topos mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], followed by derived completion and the direct-image/completion comparison, and then rationalization. Under the displayed comparisons, scalar extension of this $E$-exchange is this $E'$-exchange. The comparisons respect identity morphisms, composition, successive coefficient extensions and shifts.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E,B=\mathcal O_{E'},t=\varpi_E,v=\varpi_{E'}$. The DVR lemma gives $t=wv^e$ ($w$ a unit, $e\geq1$); the completed coefficient comparison gives $S_T\cong R_T^{[E':E]}$ as modules.

proof.text: The constructible transport lemma gives the same strata and models $S_T\otimes_B^L(B\otimes_AP)$. Ambient scalar change is exact; the inherited constructible triangles therefore give the exact integral restriction.

source.place: Assembly step 2; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Use normalized derived tensor units and associators; K-flat scalar change computes successive tensors. Both pentagon routes send $(((p\otimes s)\otimes u)\otimes z)$ to $p\otimes suz$; unit routes multiply by one. Normalize repeated fields literally to identity. The scalar adjunction is normalized by $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ on K-flat resolutions. The counit-normalized scalar-shift and balanced-associator theorems give its fixed shift compatibility. Faithful full integral inclusion and scalar localization, which is surjective on objects, detect this equation. Conjugating by the specified normalization isomorphisms gives the literal-stage associator shift equation.

source.place: Assembly step 3; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Tensor is semilinear: $C(af)=aC(f)$. Since $t=wv^e$ is invertible after inverting $v$, semilinear localization gives the exact raw rational functor and retains these equations.

source.place: Assembly step 4; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Use coefficient inverse image on each edge. The finite-free direct-image theorem gives the invertible counit-tensor mate $\beta_f$ in $D(S)$, with its shifts and coefficient towers. Ringed pushforward preserves completeness; the constant-completion equivalence identifies the convention.

source.place: Assembly step 5; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Strict-tower transport applies to augmented Koszul towers with connecting maps and units, giving unit-normalized $\kappa:C\Lambda_R\cong\Lambda_SC$. Ordinary balancing followed by $\kappa^{-1}$ gives the completed pull square. The new scalar-shift lemma gives the ordinary pull shift equation. The push mate is the composite of the derived adjunction unit, $Rg_S(\theta Rg_R)$ and $Rg_S(C_X\varepsilon_R)$; each respects shifts by derived-adjunction compatibility and whiskering. Completion transport and pasting give the completed-pull shift equation.

source.place: Assembly step 6; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Ordinary balancing and its composition law give the pull cube; mate pasting gives push composition and identities; reflection carries squares to complete objects. For completed composition precompose both scalar routes with $u=\gamma_hL_h(\gamma_g)$; naturality and the $\kappa$ unit equation reduce to ordinary composition. The quotient-tower compositor theorem gives $\widehat a\,u=\gamma_{gh}a$ ($\widehat a,a$ invertible), so $u$ cancels into complete objects.

source.place: Assembly step 7; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: Coefficient-exchange mates applied to this pull cube and its specified push mates identify the ordinary ambient exchanges after scalar extension.

source.place: Assembly step 8; retained argument and extraction map in report.md.

proof.text: The reflected-square normalization for $\beta,\gamma,\kappa$ identifies completion of this exchange with the specified completed exchange, including its direct-image/completion arrow. Restrict whenever constructibility is preserved; semilinear localization retains every equation.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, derived scalar extension is an exact
functor
$$
 T_{E'/E}=E'\otimes_E^L-:
 \Dbc(T,E)\longrightarrow\Dbc(T,E').
$$
Choose $T_{E/E}=\operatorname{id}$ literally. For $E\subset E'\subset E''$,
derived tensor associativity gives a specified exact natural isomorphism
$$
 a_{E'',E',E}:T_{E''/E'}T_{E'/E}
 \xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E''/E}.
$$
These associators satisfy the unit equations and the pentagon for four
nested fields. Exactness supplies natural shift comparisons
$$
 \sigma_{E'/E,K}:T_{E'/E}(K[1])
 \xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{E'/E}K)[1]
$$
which commute with the associators.

There are coherent natural isomorphisms
$$
 E'\otimes_E^LRf_{*,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Rf_{*,E'}(E'\otimes_E^LK)
$$
and analogous isomorphisms for pullback. Under these isomorphisms, scalar
extension of the $E$-exchange map is the $E'$-exchange map.
